comment: The defaults coai uses for a repository that has no .coai/toolchain.yaml (epoch 3 E4, SPEC section A3). EMBEDDED in coai-mcp (src_mcp/core/Toolchain/ToolchainDefaults.cs): nothing reads this file from a repository or the data folder at run time. Every argv is started WITHOUT a shell. An argv item may hold only {jobs}, {unit} and, in a format step, {file}; no item is ever copied from a manifest. Every argv below is a command that story s1 saw work INSIDE the check unit of E2 (RESULTS_s1_dotnet.md, RESULTS_s1_node.md, RESULTS_s1_format.md); a step with the host network names the heading of the RESULTS file that measured why. There is no default testFor. A step that is null does not exist for the stack. presence names are recorded by name and object id and never read (a changed one is a change of the check definition: CheckDefinition compares them); definitionFiles are read because a change of one is a change of the checks. php, rust, python and java are known and not built: their manifests are refused by name.

frozen.comment: The CLASSIFIER of the report "what the head changed in the definitions of the checks" (E4 s3; owner decision 2026-11-26: a coder job's head is REPORTED, never refused — the head's own definitions run). Before that decision this was the interim gate 'frozen build definitions'. A path the head added, deleted, modified or mode-changed against the base is called a definition or configuration file in the envelope and the job's record unless it is a plain SOURCE file: its extension (the last one, without case) is in allowedSourceExtensions AND its base name does not match configNamePattern (a regular expression, without case) AND it is not on a name list below; a symlink or a submodule is counted apart. A rename is a delete and an add. The three name lists below are the older classifier and the documentation of what the others stand for: a pattern is matched against the file name WITHOUT case at any depth; a pattern with a '/' is matched against the last segments of the path; '*' stands for any run of characters inside one name. This is the one list: no code names these files.
